verdict.rationale: Qdrant makes it easy to stand up isolated test instances separate from production. Options include a one-line local Docker run, an in-memory mode community users compare to sqlite for proofs of concept, a free-forever 1GB cloud cluster that needs no credit card, and the embedded Qdrant Edge. Snapshots and read-only or per-collection scoped API keys add ways to copy data and limit access, but the docs never present any of this as a sandbox or staging feature, so isolation relies on the user's own setup. Missing for 10: a documented first-party sandbox/staging environment or data-branching feature, a documented workflow for seeding a test environment from production (e.g., via snapshots), and hands-on evidence of agents testing safely in isolation.
